reason: E2 directly demonstrates that a phase inversion from continuous B2 to continuous BCC with discrete B2 precipitates improves ductility in a related RHEA, supporting the mechanism and predicted plasticity improvement. However, the cited evidence does not address whether the specific thermal treatment proposed will produce this inversion in the distinct NbZrTiHfMo alloy, nor does it provide data to support the quantitative predictions of ≥50% plasticity increase and ≤10% strength retention for this system.
premises: Phase inversion from continuous B2 + discrete BCC to continuous BCC + discrete B2 improves ductility while retaining strength in a related RHEA.
The proposed annealing treatment (1400 °C solutionizing + 600 °C/120 h) can induce such a phase inversion in equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
A continuous BCC matrix with discrete ordered precipitates will improve plasticity by at least 50% relative to the as-cast state.
The yield strength will remain within ~10% of 1719 MPa after the treatment.
